title: Company OKR Costed Roadmap + Escalation Simulator
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary:
Build an interactive, company-level OKR Roadmap view that combines initiative ownership, committed capacity (FTE/GPU/Reserved), estimated cost impact, and an escalation simulator that shows downstream effects when initiatives slip or capacity is constrained. Purpose is to provide execs and cross-functional PMs a single pane for: 1) making trade-offs with cost and delivery visibility, 2) predicting OKR attainment under different resource scenarios, and 3) driving consistent escalation & mitigation workflows.

Background:
Our current OKR tracking is text-heavy and disconnected from roadmap capacity and cost models. Teams repeatedly surface last-minute conflicts (e.g., Dedicated capacity vs. new model onboarding) and finance asks for impact-by-initiative cost modeling. This hub will reduce ad-hoc decisions and make the trade-offs explicit before quarter commitments.

Goals:
- Create a company-level Roadmap UI that displays OKRs, linked initiatives, owners, committed capacity (GPU hours, engineering points), and estimated monthly cost.
- Add an "Escalation Simulator" allowing PMs to simulate: delays, shaved scope, capacity reallocation; output shows OKR score delta and incremental cost/savings.
- Provide an approvals/mitigation runbook tied to simulated outcomes (auto-suggest mitigations: scope reduction, deferral, add temporary Dedicated capacity).

Success metrics:
- Reduction in cross-team capacity conflicts flagged in weekly triage by 60% in Q2.
- 80% of exec-level decisions to re-prioritize include a simulator snapshot attached to the meeting notes by end of Q2.
- Finance uses the hub for cost projections for at least 3 major initiatives in the next planning cycle.

Scope (in-scope):
- Backend: data model to join OKRs -> initiatives -> ownership -> capacity commitments -> cost model (reserved, on-demand, embeddings, token compute).
- Frontend: interactive roadmap UI with filters (by objective, org, timeframe), simulation controls, and an export snapshot.
- Workflow: config for escalation thresholds and templated mitigation playbooks.

Non-goals:
- Full HR resource allocation system (this will rely on committed capacity inputs from teams).
- Detailed per-token model costing down to microsecond kernels; use aggregated cost profiles produced by Optimize team.

Proposal & Design decisions:
- Use existing Optimize cost model API (ENG-3120) to derive baseline cost-per-initiative. Trade-off: faster launch vs. later more granular model-level costing.
- Roadmap view will be served from a normalized "initiative snapshot" service; reuse the Console config endpoints for auth and role-based views.
- Escalation simulation will run deterministic scenarios (delay X weeks, reduce scope Y%) and compute outputs with a rules engine implemented in the PM service; future version can use Monte Carlo for risk distributions.

Trade-offs considered:
- Tight coupling to payroll/FTE data increases accuracy but slows delivery; we will accept approximate committed points from teams for MVP.
- Building complex Monte Carlo risk engine vs deterministic simulator: choose deterministic MVP to get predictable, explainable outputs for exec reviews.

Rollout Plan:
1) Week 1-3: Data model + ingestion (commitments from teams, cost model integration).
2) Week 4-6: Roadmap UI MVP and snapshot export.
3) Week 7-8: Escalation simulator + templated mitigation library.
4) Week 9: Pilot with Growth, Infra, and Research PMs.
5) Week 10-12: Iterate, incorporate feedback, and present to Exec Review for Q2 gate.

Stakeholders:
- PM lead: Samir Patel (assignee)
- Eng (data & API): Priya Rao, ENG infra (ENG-1842)
- Design: Marisol Vega (UI mocks)
- Finance: Jordan Park (cost review)
- Legal/Security: Claire Dumont (privacy review if any personnel data used)

Dependencies:
- Costing API from Optimize (ENG-3120 / PM-314159)
- Console auth views for role-based filtering (ENG-2201)
- Dataset of committed capacity per initiative (teams to provide matrix by 2026-03-18)

Open questions:
- Level of fidelity for cost model required by Finance to sign off? (Jordan to confirm)
- Should the hub allow temporary capacity purchases (yes/no) or only recommend them?
- Which OKR scoring rubric to use for simulated outcome impact (current rubric vs proposed modified weights)?

acceptance_criteria: Roadmap UI displays all company-level objectives and linked initiatives with ownership and committed capacity fields populated.
Simulator can run at least three scenario types (delay, scope reduce, capacity add) and produce OKR score delta + monthly cost delta.
Snapshot export (PDF + CSV) includes simulator inputs and outputs and is attachable to decision notes.
Pilot feedback collected from at least 3 cross-functional PMs and Finance, and critical issues logged for next sprint.
